source.reported_origin: Dynamo's backend-independent KV-aware router could not reconstruct vLLM block identity from engine-specific hashes when equal multimodal placeholder tokens represented different images. Review expanded the required identity material to cache salt, LoRA, and compact prompt-embedding range hashes, and identified null-block alignment as a consumer correctness boundary.

behaviors: BlockStored exposes optional per-block identity material without changing existing fields
multimodal identifiers remain distinct for equal placeholder token sequences and align per emitted block
cache salt, LoRA identity, and mixed identity inputs preserve their block ordering
prompt embeddings use stable compact per-range fingerprints rather than tensor payloads
null physical blocks do not change the number of identity entries relative to emitted hashes
incremental caching preserves the logical parent and only emits newly stored blocks
an external consumer can reconstruct emitted block hashes from token blocks and identity material
msgpack batches preserve event types, order, existing fields, and extra keys
verifier_contract.collection_integrity: JUnit must contain at least 19 passing, unique, non-skipped cases including null alignment, compact embeddings, msgpack, and hidden mixed reconstruction.

real_lifecycle_boundary.kind: real Request hashing and BlockPool cache emission through the production ZMQ event publisher to a msgpack-decoding subscriber
real_lifecycle_boundary.entrypoint: Request -> get_request_block_hasher -> BlockPool.cache_full_blocks -> KVEventBatch -> ZmqEventPublisher -> ZMQ SUB -> msgspec decode
real_lifecycle_boundary.limitation: This feature ends at CPU scheduler metadata and event transport, so the complete production boundary is exercised without loading model weights or running a GPU model runner.
